what: Population Genetics Statistics and Selection Scan Utilities
title: Population Genetics Statistics and Selection Scan Utilities
text: PopGenR R package common population genetics workflows VCF PLINK-style genotype data. includes helpers allele frequencies, heterozygosity, nucleotide diversity, Watterson’s theta, Tajima’s D, linkage disequilibrium, PLINK quality control, runs homozygosity, annotation genomic regions single positions gene names.

title: Population Genetics Statistics and Selection Scan Utilities
text: Read VCF files analysis-ready data frames read.vcf(). Summarize genotype counts, allele frequencies, minor allele frequency, expected heterozygosity. Calculate diversity statistics nucleotide diversity, Dxy, Watterson’s theta, Tajima’s D. Calculate pooled heterozygosity (Hetp()) across genomic windows. Calculate pairwise linkage disequilibrium (calc_r2()). Run PLINK QC/PCA (plQC()) runs homozygosity (RunHom()). Annotate ranges (AnnoRan()) single positions (AnnoSin()) gene annotation data.

title: Population Genetics Statistics and Selection Scan Utilities
text: Install development version GitHub: PopGenR imports data.table, dplyr, ggplot2, vcfR. Reading GFF/GTF annotation files AnnoRan() also requires rtracklayer, Bioconductor package:

title: Population Genetics Statistics and Selection Scan Utilities
text: Annotate genomic intervals annotation data frame: Run window-based statistics VCF: Run PLINK QC PCA: PLINK helpers can use local development copy extdata/plink/plink.exe present, can pass plink_path = "path//plink" use PLINK installation.
code: library(PopGenR)  genotypes <- c("0/0", "0/1", "1/0", "1/1", "./.")  counts <- count.genotypes(genotypes) counts  allele.freq(counts) expected.het(genotypes) regions <- data.frame(   chr = c("1", "1"),   start = c(1000, 5000),   end = c(2000, 6500) )  genes <- data.frame(   chromosome_name = c("1", "1"),   start_position = c(1200, 5500),   end_position = c(1800, 6000),   external_gene_name = c("GeneA", "GeneB") )  AnnoRan(regions, CHR = "chr", starP = "start", endP = "end", annotation = genes) tajima <- TajimaD("path/to/sample.vcf", window_size = 150000) hp <- Hetp("path/to/sample.vcf", window_size = 150000) p <- plQC(file = "path/to/plink_prefix", maf = 0.05, chrset = 30) p

text: function first calculates total number valid genotypes subtracting missing data (`NN`) total genotype count. computes frequency dominant allele `` (`p`) recessive allele `` (`q`) using formula: $$p = \frac{(2 \times \text{AA count}) + \text{Aa count}}{2 \times \text{total count}}$$ $$q = 1 - p$$

text: function calculates linkage disequilibrium (LD) measure, \(R^2\), two genetic variants based genotypes. function uses allele frequencies two variants haplotype frequencies compute \(R^2\), quantifies non-random association alleles two loci.

title: calc_r2: Calculate Linkage Disequilibrium (R²) Between Two Variants — calc_r2
text: function extracts genotypes (`GT`) variants using helper function `get.field`, parses genotype data variant vectors. calculates allele frequencies `pA` `pB` variants using `allele.freq` function. haplotype frequencies determined using `get.haplotypes` function, , \(R^2\) value calculated using formula: $$D = p_{AB} - (p_A \times p_B)$$ $$R^2 = \frac{D^2}{p_A \times (1 - p_A) \times p_B \times (1 - p_B)}$$

text: numeric value representing \(D_{xy}\) value. `perBP` `TRUE`, value normalized per base pair, otherwise returns raw \(D_{xy}\) value.

title: dnuc: Calculate Nucleotide Diversity (Dxy) Between Two Populations — dnuc
text: function works first extracting genotype data (`GT`) VCF files using `get.field` function. calculates allele frequencies (`p`) variant populations using `allele.freq`. \(D_{xy}\) measure computed using formula: $$D_{xy} = \sum{p_1(1 - p_2) + p_2(1 - p_1)}$$ \(p_1\) \(p_2\) allele frequencies population 1 population 2, respectively. `perBP` `TRUE`, function calculates total number base pairs covered variants returns \(D_{xy}\) normalized number.

title: dnuc: Calculate Nucleotide Diversity (Dxy) Between Two Populations — dnuc

text: function uses following formulas compute variance: $$a1 = \sum_{=1}^{n-1} \frac{1}{}$$ $$a2 = \sum_{=1}^{n-1} \frac{1}{^2}$$ calculates coefficients \(b1\), \(b2\), \(c1\), \(c2\) based sums, finally computes variance using: $$var = e1 \cdot S + e2 \cdot S \cdot (S - 1)$$ \(e1\) \(e2\) derived \(c1\) \(c2\).
